turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning. Observations first, then the doctor will see you.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, lovely. We were stuck forever at the robot by the garage. Load shedding, lights dead, everyone hooting.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He coughed from the house to here. I'm his wife. I booked this.
[SEG0004] person_1 (NURSE): Arm straight, please. Blood pressure is one thirty-eight over eighty-four, pulse eighty-eight, oxygen ninety-seven percent, and temperature thirty-six point eight.
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): That pressure ok? I've been on the tablet for ages. My girl keeps telling me to walk, but she's at varsity doing teaching, she forgets what depot shifts are like.
[SEG0006] person_1 (NURSE): Doctor can go through that with you. Head on in.
[SEG0007] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sit. What can I do for you?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): It's the cough. Started after the flu, and it's six weeks now. I counted it from the long weekend.
[SEG0009] person_4 (DOCTOR): Worse at a particular time?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Night time, ja. Soon as I lie down it gets hectic. Daytime at the depot I cope, I just step out the office.
[SEG0011] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He wakes me every night. I thought it would fade after the flu. It hasn't.
[SEG0012] person_4 (DOCTOR): Phlegm?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): No. It's a dry cough.
[SEG0014] person_4 (DOCTOR): Fever?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No, not now. When the flu hit I was burning up and my whole body was sore, but that settled after a few days. The cough is the bit that stayed.
[SEG0016] person_4 (DOCTOR): Chest pain?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0018] person_4 (DOCTOR): Short of breath on walking?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I get to the spaza without stopping. Mind you, the bread price there is a joke now.
[SEG0020] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any blood in the cough?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing like that.
[SEG0022] person_4 (DOCTOR): Weight loss?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): No, I haven't lost any weight.
[SEG0024] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): His work trousers are hanging off him. I had to put a tuck in last week.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, actually, ja, they are loose. I have come down a bit. I only noticed when she said.
[SEG0026] person_4 (DOCTOR): Recent travel, or contact with TB?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I haven't been anywhere, and I don't know anyone with TB.
[SEG0028] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): That's not quite true. We went to his cousin in KZN in March. The clinic was treating him for TB. He was coughing right there in the lounge.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Ag, it was a quick stop, I dropped a cake for the old lady and we left. I don't believe it was TB. Nobody told me that.
[SEG0030] person_4 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Quit eight years ago. Was a pack a day on the long-haul run, Durban to Jo'burg, and I stopped when our girl was born. Best decision, besides the wedding, on a good day.
[SEG0032] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): On a good day, he says. Don't start.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm joking, doc. She's a saint. Mostly.
[SEG0034] person_4 (DOCTOR): Tablets?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Amlodipine five milligrams, one in the morning, for my blood pressure. Been years.
[SEG0036] person_4 (DOCTOR): Every single day, no misses?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose.
[SEG0038] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any antibiotic for this?
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Clinic gave me amoxicillin at the start of the flu. Five hundred milligrams three times a day for five days. Finished the whole box. Cough didn't care.
[SEG0040] person_4 (DOCTOR): Previous chest X-ray?

[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, about four years back, day hospital. They said it was borderline. Didn't give me a figure, just borderline, and I never followed up. I had to renew the truck licence, the queue was mad that week.
[SEG0042] person_4 (DOCTOR): Borderline in what way?
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): I honestly don't know. That's all they said. Borderline. Then they sent me home.
[SEG0044] person_4 (DOCTOR): Let me listen.
[SEG0045] person_4 (DOCTOR): Chest is clear. No crackles and no wheeze. Your throat looks fine.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): So is it my heart? The neighbour's cough was his heart, he landed in hospital. He still hasn't paid me for that bakkie tyre, but anyway.
[SEG0047] person_4 (DOCTOR): I'm not putting a name on this. No guessing today.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): Ok. What then?
[SEG0049] person_4 (DOCTOR): I want a chest X-ray. I'll order it for today.
[SEG0050] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And we come back when?
[SEG0051] person_4 (DOCTOR): Come back in one week and we'll go through the film.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): Can I still work the depot shifts?
[SEG0053] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yes, carry on working. If you get short of breath, a fever, or you cough up blood, come straight in. Don't wait out the week.
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): More antibiotics in the meantime?
[SEG0055] person_4 (DOCTOR): No. Keep taking the amlodipine as it is. I'm not starting anything new today.
[SEG0056] person_1 (NURSE): If the form is done I can book that chest X-ray at radiology before you go.
[SEG0057] person_4 (DOCTOR): It'll be ready at the desk. One week here for the result.
[SEG0058] person_2 (PATIENT): One week. Ja. We'll try be on time if the robots are actually working.
[SEG0059] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll make sure he comes. And I'll bring the old clinic card if I can find it in the drawer. It's a mess in there since the move.
[SEG0060] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, if we find that old clinic card we'll bring it. The hall cupboard is still packed from the move two years ago, shame.
[SEG0061] person_4 (DOCTOR): The card would help if you find it, but don't delay the X-ray for it.
[SEG0062] person_2 (PATIENT): Right. Thanks, hey. We'll see you in a week.

features: test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.

bad.reason: This is contact/exposure history in a cousin, not the patient's family history.
Past chest X-ray and borderline recollection supported; not completed now and not requested by patient.
